name: Compliance officer or regulator
oneLine: KYC, KYB, KYA, AML, consumer protection, AI rules.
goals: Map each party in an agent payment to an existing regulated role, or document the gap.
Define what Know Your Agent must mean in practice: who is accountable for an agent and what records exist.
Keep sanctions screening and AML monitoring working when the payer is a wallet address and the initiator is a model.
Protect consumers' rights to dispute, refund and revoke under Regulation E, Regulation Z, PSD2 and their successors.
Apply AI Act transparency obligations and record-keeping to agents that make purchases.
Produce audit evidence: who authorized what, when, with which constraints.
pains: Regulation E's definition of unauthorized transfer turns on whether the consumer furnished the access device, and delegation to an agent sits right on that line.
Stablecoin rules (the GENIUS Act, MiCA) say nothing about agents, and facilitators that never hold funds fall between categories.
Agent registries record identifiers, not legal persons, and most entries are placeholders.
AP2 and Verifiable Intent produce signed mandates, but production use is unverified anywhere, including inside UCP, so audit trails are inconsistent.
Consent is captured in different places (wallet, surface, merchant) with different retention rules.
Guidance is still arriving: a Treasury letter, FCA priorities, an HM Treasury consultation, MAS guidelines, and no CFPB rule.
decisions: Whether agent-initiated transactions require their own consent, disclosure and record-keeping policy.
Which registries, attestations or certifications count as Know Your Agent evidence.
Sanctions and AML treatment of facilitators, relays and agent wallets.
How to apply unauthorized-transaction liability when a mandate existed.
